summary: The milestone completed 11 experiments in 223.3 minutes, with 4 compute-bound experiments. The 81.7-minute synthesis-only reconciliation was the longest recorded path, while the only compute-bound entry in the bounded top-five list was the 21.23-minute dual-receipt benchmark; the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only reconciliation consumed 81.7 minutes and was the longest recorded path; the data does not isolate which reconciliation phase caused the delay.

The bounded top-five list names only one compute-bound path, the 21.23-minute dual-receipt benchmark; durations and phase causes for the other compute-bound experiments are not available, limiting diagnosis.
The GPU snapshot is not correlated to an active experiment or phase, so it cannot explain compute-bound runtime; the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle indicator remains false.
No concurrent multi-model compute task or failure to engage DualGPURunner is established by the supplied data.
improvements_suggested: Emit structured phase-level timing receipts for setup, dependency waits, execution, validation, and reconciliation on every experiment.
Assemble and validate reconciliation evidence incrementally as terminal artifacts arrive, then make final closeout consume the prepared evidence index.
Attach task-scoped GPU utilization samples to compute-bound execution intervals so an aggregate idle snapshot cannot be mistaken for task-time idling.
Record model concurrency and runner selection in each compute receipt, automatically selecting DualGPURunner only when at least two models run in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Build an incremental reconciliation evidence index and validate each input when it arrives.
Add structured per-phase timing receipts to every experiment and capstone.
Add task-correlated GPU telemetry plus model-concurrency-aware runner selection.
meta_reflection: The durations show where time accumulated but not why: neither the 81.7-minute synthesis reconciliation nor the 21.23-minute compute benchmark has a phase breakdown. Because the locked GPU-idle indicator is false and no concurrent multi-model task is identified, the evidence supports telemetry and reconciliation tooling changes but not a GPU-idle or DualGPURunner-failure claim; no measured counterfactual supports a nonzero savings estimate.
